# Claude Triage API

> A free, hands-on course for software engineers learning to build production-shaped applications with the Claude API.

The course teaches structured outputs, tool use, streaming, prompt caching, evaluations, model selection, trust boundaries, batching, rate limits, and MCP. Learners build and evaluate a TypeScript customer-support triage service for a fictional outdoor retailer.

## Intended audience

Working software engineers who know HTTP services and JSON. No ML or prior Anthropic experience is required. The main labs use TypeScript; a short Python comparison track is available.

## Start here

- [Course overview](https://triage.mlynn.dev/)
- [Start from zero](https://triage.mlynn.dev/start) — a beginner-safe first Claude API request.
- [Scenario](https://triage.mlynn.dev/docs/scenario) — why the system exists and what is at stake.
- [Concept map](https://triage.mlynn.dev/docs/concept-map) — the technical overview.
- [Labs](https://triage.mlynn.dev/docs/labs) — the complete self-paced path.
- [Interactive playgrounds](https://triage.mlynn.dev/playground) — live demonstrations with no setup.

## Course shape

Day 1 is about four hours: an evaluation baseline, first API request, structured outputs, tool use, streaming, prompt caching, and evals. Day 2 is optional and covers model choice, prompt injection and trust boundaries, batch processing, rate limits, and MCP.
